2607.25933.title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
2607.25933.paper_summary: Clinical diagnostic evaluation should not only assess whether models can provide correct diagnoses, but also reflect the realities of clinical practice, including progressive disclosure of multimodal information, dynamic updating of diagnostic hypotheses, and continuous refinement of clinical reasoning. However, existing evaluations of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) typically rely on single-turn or isolated tasks, making it difficult to fully capture the complexity of real-world clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we developed ClinMM-Bench, the largest multi-turn multimodal clinical diagnostic evaluation benchmark to date. ClinMM-Bench contains 1,089 challenging real-world clinical cases and 3,760 medical images across eight specialties. We systematically evaluated 15 representative MLLMs using a two-level evaluation framework that assessed both diagnostic accuracy and diagnostic reasoning quality. Results showed that proprietary models achieved the highest overall diagnostic accuracy, but the proportion of completely correct diagnoses remained limited across all models. In terms of diagnostic reasoning quality, current models can identify plausible diagnostic directions but still have considerable limitations in generating reliable diagnostic reasoning. Error analysis further identified five representative failure modes: information synthesis failure, knowledge mapping error, perception error, premature closure, and visual hallucination.
2607.25933.paper_summary_zh: 臨床診斷評估不僅應評估模型是否能提供正確的診斷，還應反映臨床實踐的現實，包括逐步披露多模態信息、動態更新診斷假設以及持續完善臨床推理。然而，現有的多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）評估通常依賴單回合或孤立任務，這使得難以充分捕捉現實世界臨床診斷的複雜性。為了彌補這一差距，我們開發了ClinMM-Bench，迄今為止最大的多回合多模態臨床診斷評估基準。ClinMM-Bench包含1,089個具有挑戰性的現實世界臨床案例和3,760幅來自八個專科的醫學影像。我們使用一個兩級評估框架系統地評估了15個代表性的MLLMs，該框架評估了診斷準確性和診斷推理質量。結果顯示，專有模型達到了最高的整體診斷準確性，但所有模型的完全正確診斷比例仍然有限。在診斷推理質量方面，當前模型能夠識別合理的診斷方向，但在生成可靠的診斷推理方面仍然存在相當大的局限性。錯誤分析進一步確定了五種代表性的失敗模式：信息綜合失敗、知識映射錯誤、感知錯誤、過早結論和視覺幻覺。
